text: Vakhtang Tsintsadze - The Asian Development Bank report highlights Georgia's attractive business environment, as well as ongoing infrastructure projects, including in the port and railway sectors.

The Asian Development Bank has published the Asian Economic Outlook report, according to which economic growth in 2025 was quite high – 7.5 percent, while in 2026, against the background of ongoing conflicts, the Asian Development Bank expects economic growth in Georgia to be 5.5 percent, which is an improved figure by 0.5 percentage points compared to the previous year's forecast, – the Deputy Minister of Economy and Sustainable Development, Vakhtang Tsintsadze, stated.
As the Deputy Minister noted, the Asian Development Bank focuses on the reduction of the current account deficit to a record low level, as well as the record high level of international reserves.
According to Vakhtang Tsintsadze, in 2026, the Asian Development Bank expects the average inflation rate in Georgia to be 3.8 percent, which is a decreased figure compared to the previous year.

“The Asian Development Bank also emphasizes that Georgia aspires to become a trade, logistics, and transport hub. In this direction, attention is focused on numerous reforms that contribute to, among others, the improvement of customs and other procedures. The Bank also highlights the infrastructural achievements that Georgia possesses in both port and railway directions,” – stated Vakhtang Tsintsadze.

According to the Deputy Minister of Economy, the ADB report highlights the attractive business environment in Georgia, focusing on the free trade agreements that Georgia possesses, as well as the mechanisms that ensure investor protection, which ultimately increases the confidence of both local and international investors and the attractiveness of Georgia.
